## Implementation plan: report and delete `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-21-3.md`

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md`
Scope-mode justification: The issue names exactly two file operations: delete one source doc and add an entry to the existing processing report, in the format of the existing `### \`analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-20.md\`` entry. Reuse is by format. The new section copies the bullet style of the 2026-09-20 entry, and the doc is added to the existing "Processed source docs" list; no new structure is introduced. No code, workflow or test changes are needed. All four sibling changelog fragments are already on `orchestrator/project-7640`, so no verdict needs to move from applied to rejected. Widening scope (other analysis docs, or new tooling) is explicitly forbidden by the issue and by the `apply_analysis_on_main.sh` scope prompt.

Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-7640` at `52c8aad116c1b933627a9dd66ac6279a21a9667e` (integration branch mismatch: false).

## Functions or modules to implement
None. Documentation-only edits:

1. **Delete** `analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-21-3.md`. Touch no other `analysis/` file. In particular, do not touch `analysis/last_collection_timestamp.txt`, `analysis/validation-selftest-status.json`, or the other `workflow-optimization-*.md` docs.

2. **Edit** `analysis/recommendation-processing-report.md`. Make additions only, and do not reflow or reword any earlier entry.
   - Line 5: change `## Processed source docs (123)` to `## Processed source docs (124)`. I counted 123 `- \`analysis/...\`` bullets in that list.
   - In the list, insert `- \`analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-21-3.md\`` directly after the last entry, `- \`analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-21-2.md\`` (around line 130), before the blank line and the `## Downstream local issue ID recheck` heading.
   - At the end of the file (after the current last line, `- Clarify/plan structured skip reasons — already-implemented (\`AI_PHASE_GATE_V1\`).`), append a blank line and then:
     - the heading `### \`analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-09-21-3.md\``
     - the line `Processed: 2026-10-19` (today's UTC date; use the actual UTC date at implement time if it differs)
     - one bullet per recommendation, in the existing style ``- <ID / label> (<short gloss>) — <verdict>: <reason>; `changelog.d/<fragment>.md` ``.

     The existing file separates the 2026-09-20 entry from the next one with a `---` line. Follow what the file does just before the end (the most recent entries) for any separator. If the last entry has none, use only a blank line.

3. **Bullets to write.** Recheck each `applied` one on the branch right before writing it. All four fragments are present today.
   - SHELL-001 — applied: pipefail truncation (`changelog.d/wfopt-2026-09-21-3-pipefail-truncation.md`).
   - CONSIST-001 — applied: `gh_api_safe` retries transient errors on read calls only (`changelog.d/wfopt-2026-09-21-3-gh-api-safe-transient.md`).
   - Reliability 4 (recursive telemetry ingestion) — applied: markers are counted only at line start (`changelog.d/wfopt-2026-09-21-3-telemetry-anchoring.md`).
   - DEAD-001 — applied: unused ledger variables removed (`changelog.d/wfopt-2026-09-21-3-ledger-dead-vars.md`).
   - Speed 1 / Cost 1 / Reliability 2 — rejected (obsolete): the guard is gone from `scripts/review_commit_changes.sh`, `scripts/review_autofix_step_init_runtime_workspace.sh` exports `LINKED_ISSUE_METADATA_FILE`, and `REVIEW_EDITOR_PREFLIGHT` checks the editor's preconditions before the reviewers run.
   - Speed 2 — rejected (obsolete): CI has run as parallel jobs since #4707 (about 9 minutes end to end).
   - Speed 3 — rejected: `git push --dry-run` does not exercise the server-side workflow-permission check, and a mutating probe is unsafe.
   - Speed 4 — already-implemented: `review-autofix-failure:v1` fingerprint cap (`REVIEW_FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_MAX_IDENTICAL`) and `NOOP_RECOVERY_SKIP_FINGERPRINT_CAP`.
   - Speed 5 — rejected: saves about 3 to 4 seconds, not worth the concurrency complexity.
   - Cost 2 — adaptive quorum already-implemented (`REVIEW_TIER_RESOLVER_ENABLED`, lite/standard/full, on by default); the circuit-breaker default flip is rejected, consistent with the 2026-09-20 verdict.
   - Cost 3 — rejected: automatic reduction risks dropping review evidence. `CONTEXT_BUDGET_WARN` stays advisory, and `REVIEWER_FILTER_UNINTERESTING_ENABLED` is an operator opt-in.
   - Cost 4 / Cost 5, Prompt Cache 3–5, AI Memory Health retry fields, Reliability 5 / 6 — rejected: new telemetry or features with no reader, and the cited incidents do not reproduce on current code. `SEMBLE_QUERY` already logs bytes, sources and `static_dup_bytes`, and `RELEASE_NOTIFY_V1` already reports SUPERSEDED runs.
   - Prompt Cache 1 and 2 — already-implemented: the pre-assembled static context is ordered with the stable prefix first and dynamic data appended.
   - Reliability 1 — already-implemented: `AUTOFIX_FAILURE_HEADLINE` (failed step and first `::error::` line), and the `reviewers_failed` / `sandbox_prepare_failed` reasons replace the `editor_empty_noop` masking.
   - Reliability 3 — already-implemented: `HEAD:refs/heads/${SOURCE_BRANCH}` is used in both `mark-stable.yml` and `test-and-mark-stable.yml`; the extra classifier is rejected as low value.
   - GH API audit (E2E polling interval, per-call `GH_API_CALL` logging, failure-handler consolidation) — rejected: the release gate already polls with `POLL_INTERVAL: 10` and the cited 5-second loop could not be found; per-call logging duplicates `GH_API_RETRY`; there is no call-count evidence for the failure handlers.
   - `ORCHESTRATOR_CYCLE_SUMMARY` / `HEAL_SKIP` — rejected: new telemetry with no reader; `WORKFLOW_HEAL skip reason=` already exists.
   - API-001, API-002, API-003, BATCH-001 — rejected: tagged RISKY_SKIP in the source doc.
   - MERGE-001, MERGE-004, MERGE-005, MERGE-006 — rejected: RISKY_SKIP in the source doc.
   - MERGE-002, MERGE-003 — rejected: NEEDS_VERIFICATION, small call savings, and both are fail-closed lint gates whose per-item error behaviour is pinned by tests.
   - DUP-001 — rejected: `semble_helpers.sh` is in `OPTIONAL_BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPTS` and is not sourced by `review_apply_fixes.sh` / `review_conflict_prepare.sh`, so every caller would still need a fallback copy.
   - DUP-002 — rejected: a new shared module would have to be staged into every support copy, and the existing `_parse_iso8601` signatures differ.
   - EXPR-001 — already-implemented: the implement.yml "Stage workflow support files" `run:` body has no `${{ }}`; both interpolations sit in `env:`.
   - DEAD-002 — already-implemented: `BRANCH_REBUILD_THRESHOLD_DECISION` logs `skip_reason` and `last_rebuild_at`.

   If a fragment is missing at implement time (the matching sibling PR was reverted or never merged into `orchestrator/project-7640`), record that item as `rejected: not landed on the integration branch (<actual reason, e.g. sibling issue #N closed unmerged>)` instead of `applied`.

## Decisions
### D1 — No changelog fragment for this PR
- Chosen: no `changelog.d/` fragment. The four sibling PRs already carry the user-visible changelog entries.
- Alternatives considered: add a docs-only fragment saying the analysis doc was processed.
- Why: this PR only changes internal `analysis/` bookkeeping, with no behaviour change for consumers. A fragment would duplicate the sibling entries, and the issue names exactly two files.

### D2 — Delete the doc and list it in the report in the same commit
- Chosen: one commit/PR that deletes the source doc and adds it to the report.
- Alternatives considered: update the report first and delete the doc in a separate PR.
- Why: `scripts/apply_analysis_on_main.sh` warns and skips a doc that is listed in the report but still exists (line 328–329). Doing both together keeps that state from ever existing on `main`.

### D3 — Verify each applied verdict on the branch, not from the decomposition snapshot
- Chosen: check that each `changelog.d/wfopt-2026-09-21-3-*.md` fragment exists on `orchestrator/project-7640` before writing `applied`.
- Alternatives considered: copy the verdicts from the issue as they stand.
- Why: the issue requires it, and a sibling PR that did not land would otherwise be reported as applied.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundaries: none touched. No workflow, script, prompt or credential path changes.
- Authorization: no new endpoint or surface.
- External input: the source doc is model-generated analysis text. Do not copy instructions or commands from it into the report, only the verdicts listed above.
- Abuse cases: not applicable. Keep secrets, tokens and run-log excerpts out of the report text.
